protocol: Two fresh blind @vision reads per repo on the 1440x900 final frame; one image per task; no source, no sibling views, no expected answer; describe-first then strict JSON {question_answered, action, blockers, confidence}. The image self-identifies as a Perfpal weight map; the reads are blind to the other candidate and to the source.
animation: CSS keyframes only; final frame captured with prefers-reduced-motion; the artifact contains no JavaScript.

cJSON.description: This is a "Perfpal weight map" for the cJSON codebase: a static-cost treemap with a findings brief underneath. The header shows repo stats (101 files · 1055 functions · 837 findings · parse 63 ok / 38 partial / 0 failed) and a Pause button. The headline immediately states the story: "93.5% of static weight is test code (tests/unity/test/tests); production is only 0.2%. Start in production: PERF-C-LOOP-002 at cJSON_Utils.c:1188 (hot/medium), led by core (root)." The treemap itself is almost entirely one giant hatched rectangle labelled "tests/unity/test/tests" (93.5% · 2.00M static cost units (v2) · ≈53,354× median components), plus a narrow "tests" strip (6.2% of map, badge 2) and a few tiny unlabeled cells clumped in the bottom-right corner — area and colour encode static cost units (v2), and the hatch pattern covers test/bench/other code. Because the test cell dwarfs everything, the production cells (0.2% of cost) are effectively invisible as slivers. Below the map, a "KV1 BRIEF — top 4 actions, production first, ranked by severity then confidence" shows four cards: (1) HOT/MEDIUM `cJSON_Utils.c:1188` "Expensive setup or I/O call inside loop" ('sprintf' runs every iteration at loop depth 1; 1.05k cost units · 524.0× median function), (2) WARN/HIGH `cJSON.c:127` "Unbounded string operation" via 'sprintf' (2.60k · 1,302×), (3) WARN/HIGH `cJSON.c:703` "High cyclomatic complexity" ('utf16_literal_to_utf8' branches 17 ways, threshold 15; 2.60k · 1,302×), and (4) WARN/HIGH `fuzzing/afl.c:163` "Deallocation inside loop" ('free' at loop depth 1; 81 · 40.5×). A footer offers "Q2 · what depends on the hot component? Open the 1-hop drill →" and notes "124/229 unresolved + 9 non-repo imports excluded from drill". What stands out: the weight distribution is so skewed toward test code that the map's visual answer is essentially "the tests drown everything," and the actionable answer comes from the brief cards, not from reading the rectangles.

json.question_answered: Where is the static weight concentrated, and which top 4 actions should I take first (production first, ranked by severity then confidence)?
json.action: Fix PERF-C-LOOP-002 at cJSON_Utils.c:1188 — hoist the 'sprintf' call out of the loop (it runs every iteration at loop depth 1) or batch its work, as the headline recommends 'Start in production: PERF-C-LOOP-002 at cJSON_Utils.c:1188 (hot/medium)'
json.blockers: The treemap is unreadable for production code: the tests/unity/test/tests cell occupies 93.5% of the area, so the production cells (0.2% of cost) are tiny unlabeled slivers in the bottom-right corner; the actionable answer comes from the KV1 BRIEF cards rather than from the map geometry. Also 'production static cost units (v2)' legend swatches are unlabelled by value.

hyperfine.description: This is a Perfpal "weight map" (a treemap) for the project hyperfine, summarizing where static-analysis cost concentrates across 53 files / 335 functions / 348 findings (parse 53 ok / 0 partial / 0 failed). The headline answers the question outright: "src is the heaviest cell (35.7% of static cost); start with PERF-RS-ALLOC-001 at src/command.rs:148 (hot/high)." Each rectangle's area and shade of blue encode "static cost units (v2)" for production code, while diagonally hatched cells (tests, src/benchmark, scripts) are test/bench/other, excluded from the production ranking. The biggest, darkest cell is `src` at 35.7% (1.62k static cost units, 8.0× the median component); other production cells are src/export (10.4%), src/output (5.9%), src/timer (3.0%), src/quantity (2.9%), src/parameter (2.6%), plus tiny unlabeled cells at bottom-right. Below the map, a "KV1 BRIEF" ranks the top 5 actions: cards 1–3 all sit in src/command.rs (lines 148, 335, 161 — heap allocation inside a loop, `Command::new` inside a loop, `.len` recomputed in a loop), card 4 flags a module-graph cycle between src/metric.rs and src/benchmark/measurement.rs, and card 5 flags high cyclomatic complexity at src/options.rs:254 (`from_cli_arguments` branches 52 ways vs. threshold 15). Each card shows severity (HOT/WARN), confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM), a cost anchor (e.g. 611 static cost units, 87.3× median function, top 2% of files), and a truncated remediation hint. The footer offers the next step — "Q2 · what depends on the hot component? Open the 1-hop drill →" — with caveats: static heuristics, 4/238 unresolved, 29 non-repo imports excluded, ARCH-002 excluded. A Pause button sits top-right beside a small light-to-dark-blue legend for production static cost units.

tmux.description: This is a Perfpal "weight map" for the tmux codebase: a treemap where each rectangle is a source file, sized (and shaded) by its share of "static cost units (v2)". The header reports 216 files · 3189 functions · 7545 findings, with parse status "100 ok / 116 partial / 0 failed", plus a Pause button. A bold answer-first headline reads "format.c is the heaviest cell (6.8% of static cost); start with PERF-C-ALLOC-001 at compat/getline.c:85 (hot/high)." The three biggest labelled cells are format.c (badge 1, 6.83k static cost units, 2.6× median component, top 2% of cells), window-copy.c (badge 2, 5.11k, 2.0× median, top 4%), and window.c (badge 3, 3.84k, 1.5× median, top 6%), followed by compat, screen-write.c, tty.c (3.2% of map), grid.c, colour.c, etc.; a hatched grey "other (107 cells)" block swallows 17.2% of the map (16.7% of cost), and many smaller cells have truncated names ("server-clien…", "screen-redraw…"). Below the map, a "KV1 BRIEF — top 5 actions, production first, ranked by severity then confidence" lists five finding cards, each with severity chip (HOT/WARN), file:line, title, explanation, and cost footers: 1 HOT/HIGH `compat/getline.c:85` "Heap allocation inside loop" (realloc at loop depth 1, 56 units, 2.8× median function); 2 HOT/MEDIUM `tty.c:601` "Expensive setup or I/O call inside loop" (streaming write each iteration, 3.09k units, 154.4× median); 3 WARN/HIGH `format.c:336` "Deallocation inside loop" (free at loop depth 1, 6.83k units, 331.6× median); 4 WARN/HIGH `format.c:393` "High cyclomatic complexity" (format_job_get branches 17 ways, threshold 15); 5 WARN/HIGH `window-copy.c:2104` "Deeply nested loops" (nesting depth 3, 5.11k units, 255.3× median). verdict: F: 6/6 valid reads (one empty first attempt retried) state the static-weight question and one concrete path:line action from the brief. Hyperfine and tmux read strongly; cJSON is the failure case — the treemap is 93.5% test code and the production cells (0.2%) are unreadable slivers, so the brief carries the answer.
observations: O1: The KV1 brief is the reliable answer surface in all three repos; every read took its action from the brief or the headline, not from the treemap geometry.

O2: cJSON is the F failure case: a single test cell consumes 93.5% of the area; production cells are 0.2% and unreadable. This is a data/area-policy issue (test cost in the hero area), not a layout bug.
O3: Hyperfine and tmux read well: the mass cells + brief give a clear start; tmux users noted truncated small-cell labels, the hatched other block, and unlabeled legend swatches.
O4: One read misread `83,354×` as `53,354×`/`3,354×`; the artifact/manifest value is 83,354×. The error does not change the action.
O5: The brief cards' remediation hints are truncated in the visible text; one reader asked for the enclosing function name (the card shows path:line, not function).
O6: No read found a bare cost number after the unit/anchor fix.
